ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Elisabeth of Austria

code.originalText: Four-week review: weight, vital signs, electrolytes, bone density, and depression

text.paragraph: Four-week review of anorexia nervosa: weight, vital signs, electrolytes, bone density and depression. [S]

Empress Elisabeth returns three weeks after her consultation. She has had four CBT-E sessions, two in person and two by video, has seen the dietitian twice, and had a video review with Dr. Haddad-Lindström last week; her plan is now about 2,200 kcal a day. She took the phosphorus tablets for three weeks and finished thiamine. The weekly blood tests were drawn at laboratories where she stayed and were reported to the clinic as normal. She has walked about an hour a day and stopped weighing herself at home, which she found very hard. The dizziness on standing has nearly gone and the ankle swelling is less. Her mood is still low and she thinks often of her son; she has had passive thoughts of death on two days, with no intent or plan. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-03-03; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Thin; weight 49.6 kg, BMI 16.8; temperature 36.2 C
Lying blood pressure 102/66, pulse 54; standing 98/64, pulse 64; regular rhythm; trace ankle edema
Standing height 172 cm; no spinal tenderness
Mood low, affect constricted, tearful when speaking of her son; no intent or plan to harm herself

Weight loss to a body mass index of 16.0 (47.4 kg at 172 cm), about 6 kg over six months, with fatigue, swelling of both ankles, dizziness on standing, slow pulse and cold intolerance; cause not established at intake; a restrictive eating disorder suspected, with thyroid disease, celiac disease, diabetes, malignancy and adrenal insufficiency to be excluded; eating disorders psychiatry consultation requested
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to her documented restrictive eating, low weight and swelling; superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation.

Anorexia nervosa, restricting type, moderate (DSM-5-TR), with compulsive exercise and frequent self-weighing, beginning in early adulthood; complicated at diagnosis by sinus bradycardia, orthostatic dizziness, ankle edema, mild anemia and leukopenia, low glucose, raised ALT and low phosphate after refeeding began
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, linked to her documented restrictive eating and exercise and to the retrospective diagnosis of anorexia nervosa (R).
Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate, with persistent grief for her son, who died five years ago; passive thoughts of death without intent or plan at intake
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented mourning and ever-deepening depressions; not a claim that she was so diagnosed.

Low bone mass (osteopenia) of the lumbar spine and hip after decades of low weight: lumbar spine T-score -2.1, femoral neck T-score -1.8; FRAX 10-year probabilities 6.8% for a major osteoporotic fracture and 1.2% for hip fracture; no fractures
S — Synthetic modern finding on DXA; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Anorexia nervosa, restricting type, moderate, improving (F50.011). Weight up 2.2 kg in four weeks, to BMI 16.8. Medically stable: pulse 56 seated, orthostatic rise now 10, potassium 3.9 mmol/L, phosphate 3.2 mg/dL, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, glucose 80 mg/dL. Hemoglobin 11.9 g/dL and white cells 3.9 x10^3/uL are improving; ALT 38 U/L is falling. ECG: sinus rhythm 56, QTc 436 ms. [S]
Stop phosphorus tablets.
Continue the meal plan, CBT-E and the dietitian.
Electrolytes, phosphate and magnesium at each visit while underweight.
Walks of up to an hour a day; no gymnastics yet.

Low bone mass after decades of low weight (M85.80). DXA today: lumbar spine T-score -2.1, femoral neck -1.8, low bone mass. FRAX 10-year probabilities 6.8% for a major osteoporotic fracture and 1.2% for hip fracture, below the thresholds for drug treatment. Weight restoration is the main treatment. [S]
Calcium carbonate 1,250 mg daily with a meal, with dairy foods, for about 1,200 mg of calcium a day.
Continue vitamin D 2,000 IU daily; recheck 25-hydroxyvitamin D in about three months.
Repeat DXA in two years.

Recurrent depression with persistent grief (F33.1). PHQ-9 14, little changed. Nutrition is under way and the QTc is normal, so an antidepressant can start, as the consultant advised. Sertraline is chosen for its low QT risk and few interactions. [S]
Sertraline 25 mg each morning for two weeks, then 50 mg.
Nurse telephone check two weeks after starting.
Grief-focused work in CBT-E sessions.
Safety plan reviewed and unchanged; 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, the clinic number and local emergency numbers abroad confirmed.
